steps.text: Cut a deep pocket into the fat side of each pork chop, being careful not to cut all the way through. Combine bread crumbs, sugar, ground black pepper, salt, 3 tablespoons melted butter, onion, and parsley in a bowl until well mixed. Fill pork chop pockets with bread crumb mixture; secure with toothpicks.
Heat remaining 2 tablespoons melted butter in a skillet over medium heat. Cook pork chops until browned, about 5 minutes per side.

Add beef broth. Reduce heat to low and simmer, turning pork chops at least once, until tender and an instant-read thermometer inserted into the center of a chop reads at least 145 degrees F (63 degrees C), about 30 minutes.
Let pork chops rest briefly. Remove toothpicks and spoon pan juices over pork chops before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Tender Stuffed Pork Chops
raw_recipe.description: These easy stuffed pork chops are filled with savory bread crumbs and onion, then simmered in beef broth until tender for a comforting dinner.

review.reviewBody: For some reason I've always stayed away from stuffed porkchops, thinking it seemed too hard to do or that they just wouldn't taste good. I had some very thick chops and decided to go for it with this recipe. I'm glad I did because they were wonderful! I only had italian style bread crumbs but they added a very nice flavor to the stuffing. I added about 1/2 a cup more of the broth to the pan which was just enough to drizzle over the chops. I would even suggest thickening it a bit to make it more of a gravy if desired. The family loved them and were very impressed! This would be great to serve to company too. If you've never tried making stuffed chops, give this recipe a try.

I made the ACTUAL recipe. Very good, but salty! Some tips: Needs to be at least an inch thick chop. DO NOT ADD SALT - skip what recipe calls for. Cover pan. Med low, not low low. Like a 4-5 on electric stoves. The recipe had me cooking at a 3 uncovered but they were still pink after the 30 min called for. Highly recommend.
Absolutely wonderful! I did sauté the onion and celery a bit before making stuffing as suggested by reviewer. My husband said to please don’t lose this recipe. It is definitely guest worthy.

These were amazing! I'm usually a little nervous about making pork chops because they're so easy to dry out. The only change I made to this recipe was to leave out the onion and bake them instead of cooking them for the full time on the stove. I seared them on each side before putting them in a glass pan with the broth, then covered with foil and baked at 400 for 20-25 mins. I turned and basted them once. These had great flavor and weren't dried out at all!
I sautéed the onion and 1 rib of celery along with an extra 1/2 cup of broth, I used chicken, all recommended from other reviewers and it turned out great

the things I did differently was to omit the sugar and salt (I substituted garlic powder), used italian style bread crumbs, used chicken broth instead of beef (as it's all I had on hand, and it's not low sodium hence the reason I omitted the salt) and I added some grated parmesan cheese (the one you get in the bottle) to the bread crumb mixture before I stuffed the chops (about 1/4 cup) 

I only gave it a 4 because I do NOT eat pork, but my husband begged me to make pork chops, this may not have been what he had in mind but he LOVED them and I got the benefit of not having to experience the pork "after taste"
Delicious! I added small sweet peppers and finely diced baby bellas. Big tasty chop!

Been making this recipe for years always turns out great. Two tips I have 1. I cut the opening of the pocket only about 1 1/2 to 2 inches. I never have to put toothpicks in it to hold it closed and nothing has ever fallen out. I’ve enclosed a photo with the slit side showing. 2. If you have extra stuffing, you can put a little extra butter in the pan and cook up any extra stuffing that is left over for a couple of minutes, right before adding in the broth. This adds flavor to the sauce and thickens it as well. I generally add more than the cup of broth because as it’s cooking most of it evaporates and we really like the sauce.

I made these for dinner tonight and absolutely scrumptious!! Never made stuffed pork chops before but this will be on top of my list for chops! I have to say I cheated and used stove top stuffing however I used chicken broth in place of the water it called for and added sauteed onion and celery. Also added a splash of wine to the saute pan with chicken broth. Family loved it!! Thank you Karen!!

I REALLY LIKED THIS RECIPE BUT I CHANGED THE RECIPE A BIT. I DIDN'T HAVE PORK CHOPS SO I USED BONELESS LOIN CHOPS AND CUT THE CHOP IN HALF TO MAKE IT THINNER SO I COULD ROLL THE CHOPS WITH THE STUFFING INSIDE. I DIDNT HAVE TOOTH PICKS SO SOME STUFFING DID FALL OUT BUT IT WAS OKAY BECAUSE IT HELPED THE SAUCE. I FOLLOWED THE STUFFING RECIPE TO THE T BESIDES DRIED PARSLEY I ONLY HAD FRESH PARSLEY. I ADDED TURKEY BACON TO THE STUFFING AS WELL. I COOKED IT UNTIL IT AS CRUNCHY THEN CHOPPED THEM UP INTO LITTLE PEICES. ONCE I WAS DONE ROLLING THE CHOPS I ADDED THE REMAINING STUFFING ON TOP AND AFTER 5 MINUTES I ADDED THE BROTH. IT WAS REALLY YUMMY. I KNOW SOME HAD ISSUES WITH THE PORK CHOPS BECOMING CHEWY AND NOT AS TENDER. IF YOU USE MY TECHNIQUE AND USE THINNER CHOPS YOU WILL NOT HAVE THAT PROBLEM. MY HUSBAND IS BEGGING ME FOR MORE AS I TYPE. THIS RECIPE IS DEFINETLY A KEEPER! I HOPE EVERYONE ELSE ENJOYS!

This was my 1st time making stuffed pork chops and it came out very tasty! I made a few changes. For two thick cut pork chops, I used 1 cup of chicken stove top, which I ground into bread crumb texture, halved other stuffing ingredients. I first sauteed the diced onions in the butter for a few minutes then create the pork chop stuffing. Cook time important because I think if you follow the recipe directions, it's probably more likely to end up dry. I hate dry chops! I did sear each side for 4-5 min on med heat. Added about a cup of chicken broth and simmered for 10 minutes each side. Super tasty gravy, really good chops, this was a good recipe. I look forward to trying with other stuffing options! Thanks Karen.
I couldn't find plain cubed bread crumbs at the store so used seasoned. Left out the salt/pepper but followed the rest of the recipe.
Very good and easy recipe. I added some fresh chopped garlic in the stuffing and some mushrooms that I had to use. My wife loved it. Thank you for the recipe!
Made my own cornbread stuffing, and used beef gravy instead of broth - everyone loved it!

Loved this recipe! I used a cornbread stuffing mix and made a couple mistakes. I salted and peppered the chops before filling! Too salty since the beef broth was salty, the stuffing was also salty and I brined the chops to ensure their tenderness. Yes, too salty! I will not make that mistake again, BUT I will definitely make this again! However, the chops were tender, cooked through and very tasty!

Tasty recipe. Will do again. What I will say is that everyone has different tastes and kitchens. The timing for the original recipe may be different depending on how well done you want the chop and and your stove output. I have found that I have to make a dish a few times before I get to my liking.
Held together well; easy to make. Unfortunately, the onions (I chopped them very fine) were still crunchy. Plus there wasn't much flavor. My husband enjoyed these pork chops.

My two pork chops came out incredible so delicious so easy and quick made a beautiful dinner for Easter. The changes that I had made on the recipe is I fried the pork chops in olive oil for flavor and I didn't do exact measurements on the recipe . I also used extra butter for the stuffing, to make it the right consistency. I love being a member of allrecipes.com excellent app
Absolutely love this!! I’m not a cook by any means but it definitely is easy to follow and tastes great!!
